connect.title: Connect Search Console
connect.body: Clicks, impressions and positions for {site} are fetched every night once Search Console is connected. Until then no figures are shown.
connect.noSite: No public website is registered for {app}, so there is nothing to connect.
connect.ownerOnly: Only the owner can connect Search Console.
connect.step1: Create a service account in a Google Cloud project (IAM & Admin › Service accounts) and create a JSON key for it.
connect.step2: Turn on the «Google Search Console API» in the same project.
connect.step3: Add the service account's email address as a user on {site} in Search Console (Settings › Users and permissions). Restricted access is enough.
connect.keyNote: The key goes straight to the vault and is never shown again. Only the account's email address is kept visible.
connect.badKey: This is not a JSON key for a service account.
connect.connected: Search Console is connected. {mapped} of {sites} websites found, {rows} rows fetched.

meta_ads.2: Assign it your ad accounts with View performance.
meta_ads.3: Generate a token for your app with ads_read and read_insights, and paste it below.

tips.dearKeywordNone: «{name}» has {clicks} clicks and no signups in {days} days, while a signup costs {rest} on the rest — pause it and add it as a negative keyword.
tips.bestKeyword: «{name}» converts best: {cps} per signup against {rest} for the rest — raise its bid.
tips.dearAd: «{name}» costs {cps} per signup, {ratio}× the campaign’s other ads ({rest}) — move its budget to the ads that convert.
tips.dearAdNone: «{name}» has {clicks} clicks and no signups in {days} days, while a signup costs {rest} on the other ads — move its budget to the ads that convert.
tips.linkTitle: Opens {platform}, where the change is made. Sentral reads {platform} and changes nothing there.

results.title: Results per step · {name}
results.noReports: Another person’s email: its figures need Campaigns › See reports of others.
results.empty: This campaign has no email yet.
results.failed: The results could not be read.
results.note: Rates are over delivered emails. Opens count people, not the automatic opens of Apple Mail, so they are lower than the provider’s. Signups: visits from the email’s links that finished signing up.

emailTips.ab: Email {n} has a {rate} click rate in the last 30 days — test a shorter subject.
emailTips.abOff: Not available yet: an automated email cannot have an A/B subject.
emailTips.cond: {share} of email {n}’s recipients in the last 30 days had already uploaded their employee list — add a condition before it.
emailTips.time: Emails go when each wait ends; switch to «send at best time» ({days} {hour}).

best.title: Best time to send
best.subtitle: Open rate by weekday and hour
best.cellThin: {day} {hour} · too few sends ({n} of the {min} needed)
best.note: The application’s email over the last {days} days, by when it was sent (Oslo time). A time needs {min} delivered emails.
best.outside: {n, plural, one {# delivered email was} other {# delivered emails were}} sent at hours outside this grid.
best.failed: The send times could not be read.
best.button: Send all steps at the best time
best.offTitle: Press to send each email when its step is reached again.
best.onNote: Each email waits for the next of these times, the first one included.
best.noEmail: This campaign has no email to time.
best.notYet: Not yet: no time has {min} delivered emails in the last {days} days.
best.unread: Needs the send times, which could not be read.
best.toastOff: Steps send when each wait ends
